chapter: Boston, Buffalo and finding a style
title: Left-hand technique: unorthodox two-finger vibrato
summary: Stewart uses the classical position but gets vibrato or tremolo with two fingers, one fixed and one shaking, a style of his own.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, with your left hand did you use the -- now, I've seen in old photographs like, say, Pops Foster

or some of the jazz players, that instead of using the -- well, I don't know if this is exactly right, but the classical position. I've seen like jazz players where some look like they're choking the bass.
In other words --

Some of them look like they've got the bass laying flat in the palm of their hand, and they're trying to press four fingers down. Now, when -- I notice when you play, though, now, you use the classical position.
Classical position mostly. At times -- I have developed a way to play as I feel, what would you say, non-orthodox.
Like there's this picture in your head.
Yeah.
Where you've got like -- you've got your fingers -- tape recorder, this is out of this program.
Yes, right.

It's a picture of Mr. Stewart playing where he has his fingers, I don't know a way I can describe it for the tape recorder, but it's very unorthodox looking. So did you do that in order to get another, get different sounds out of the notes?
That's right, yes. Lots of times I used two fingers along with resting the other, my first two fingers.
On your left hand only.
On my left hand, to make --
The fingering note.
-- the tremolo, like, what do you call -- eh-yeh-yeh-ey-yeh-yeh-yeh.
Right.
Vibrato like.
Right.
And usually you don't use two fingers.
You shake your hand more or less, which is supposed to be orthodox, you know.
Right, like that.
Yeah, that's right.
Right.
Instead of -- but I use just two fingers, you know.
And you just finger, what do you do?
You move them rapidly against the strings like that?
Move one against -- yeah, right against -- the one stayed permanent, and the other one kind of next to it.
Oh, I see. So you sit one finger down, like your index finger, say, on the string.
That's right, and the other one.
And use your second finger, move the
second finger to get the tremolo.
That's right, yes.
All right, instead of using all four like the classical players do.
That's right.
Okay. All right.
In fact, I had my own style, more or less, you know, the way I felt it.
